doc.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

title: Leaving music for a BMG archive job and band frustrations
summary: He took a day job in the RCA Victor/BMG archive for eight years, tired of running a band alone and finding subs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: There was an interesting entry about you, I forget where I saw it, it said that you retired in
Yeah. Yeah I hung it up for a while.

I took a gig at a record company, in fact Joe Muranyi was here and it was the same company, it was the RCA Victor Company. And it was, in my time, known as BMG. Burtlesman Music Company. And I worked in the archive, which was a wonderful gig. And I had kind of had enough. I tried to run everything by myself, it’s really hard.
You’ve got so many things to contend with. And it was time.

If you had a Monday night with your band, did you have trouble because some of your musicians might have got a call for a better paying gig or something and get a phone call and like okay, now I’ve got to fill this chair. That’s very hard.

It’s very hard, it’s part of the frustration. And you know, sometimes you might get a substitute and he might be, you know a nice fellow and a good musician, but not really the person to make this meal. I look at it like everyone’s putting these ingredients into making this meal and if you don’t have the right seasoning or the right combination it’s not going to turn out as well as having the right person in there to give you the feel or give you the idiom or the understanding of what the band is about.
